speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether the Ministry will consider implementing regulations for direct-to-consumer (DTC) genetic testing services to address concerns related to privacy, accuracy and consumer protection; (b) what is the Ministry doing to enhance public awareness about the potential sharing and commercial use of genetic data obtained from DTC tests by third parties; and (c) how will individuals have access to accurate information, genetic counselling and guidance in interpreting test results to mitigate any risks of misinterpretation and unnecessary anxiety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: These risks include exaggerated claims, the possible sharing and commercial use of genetic data obtained from DTC tests by third parties and the lack of proper medical interpretation of test results.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Consumers should exercise care to assess for themselves the suitability and quality of such non-clinical tests.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Consumers need to read the test provider's terms and conditions carefully before using such tests and contact the provider or approach their doctors when in doubt.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, can the Ministry elaborate why are non-clinical genetic tests allowed to be provided directly to the consumer but not clinical genetic tests?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, for users of direct-to-consumer (DTC) genetic tests, how can they be assured that their data will not be sold to third parties, especially in cases where the tests are sold online but processed overseas?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, they are assessed to be of lower risk and may be offered directly to consumers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Nonetheless, it is important for consumers of non-clinical genetic tests to be informed and take precautions for themselves in looking after their own interests.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, that is why we have developed the guidance document and enhanced consumer education to raise awareness on genetic testing.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, they should be administered by medical practitioners with the appropriate knowledge and training.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, we make sure that the medical practitioner is involved in order to actually look at the test results properly and provide the necessary management to the individual.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In respect of the second question, because of this difference with the DTC tests, we take a risk-based approach, as I had explained.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It means that the consumer has to be responsible, has to be aware that they have to protect themselves.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Having said that, as I mentioned, we have guidelines in place.
